quote: I do want you to know I have trees, and I'm not cutting any of my trees down.
stewart_read: Customer references a prior company visit that soured him (told to cut trees); rep never asks which company or what else was said in that design.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the tree issue as fully resolved once the trim compromise landed, making further probing unnecessary — but the company identity/context is still lost for the closer.
coaching_implication: A quick 'who was that with?' would give the closer competitive context and confirm no other blockers from that visit.

quote: Okay. Wow. Yeah. Definitely. You know, it's more expensive.
stewart_read: Rep acknowledges the $331 bill as painful but files it — no flip into alignment-against-the-utility, no forward hook to what solar could do to that number.
coaching_implication: Should have flipped: 'That $331 is basically what you'd be paying the utility instead of owning your power — let's see what solar could replace that with.'

quote: It was a a few hours more than I had last year this time, so I just kinda tossed it. So I don't have that available at this time.
stewart_read: Customer hands over a usage-increase signal (higher this year) that the rep could use as an anchor, but rep only chases the document, not the trend.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically staying laser-focused on getting the raw bill data rather than editorializing mid-collection — reasonable in the moment, but the usage-increase point still goes unused later.
coaching_implication: Reflect the trend back: 'so your usage is climbing — that's exactly the kind of pattern solar offsets.'

quote: my wife's got MS, and I'm in and out. My wife is up and down, and it all depends on her.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a real caregiving burden as a trust gift explaining his unpredictable schedule; rep's response is a fast reassurance with no specific acknowledgment.
coaching_implication: A brief specific acknowledgment ('that sounds like a lot to manage — we'll work around her schedule') would land better than the generic 'No. No. You're good.'

quote: Could you give me a callback in about an hour, hour and a half? And I'll have that information for you because I have to check my wife's calendar schedule.
stewart_read: Wife is co-owner and the scheduling gatekeeper; rep accepts the deferral without proposing to include her directly or float a tentative window pending her calendar.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be reactively taking the easy out rather than strategically deferring — no evidence he intends to use the callback to lock in a joint time.
coaching_implication: Should have said 'let's pencil in Friday and confirm once you check with her' to anchor something concrete instead of an open-ended callback.

quote: I'll call you back in about an hour and a half and then kinda, you know, get a good time from you.
stewart_read: Call ends with no locked time, no verbal handshake, and no bill — a fully open-ended next step owned loosely by the rep.
coaching_implication: Even a callback should end with a specific confirmed time ('I'll call you at 6:30, does that work?') rather than a vague 'hour and a half.'
